newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to issue T$3 bln in NCDs on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to issue T$3 bln in NCDs on Friday.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank said on Friday it would issue T$3 billion in one-month negotiable certificates of deposit later in the day.
Bids will close at 3.00 pm (0700 GMT), a central bank official said.
The central bank's recent non-stop NCD issuance was seen widely in the market as aiming to keep a lid on the loose liquidity that many experts say has been fuelling the sizzling stock market rally.
Taiwan's deputy central bank governor Liang Cheng-chin on Wednesday flatly denied that this was the case, saying the bank was acting purely in response to the liquidity situation.

"The scale of the central bank's NCD issuance was determined by the liquidity situation. It has no direct or close relation with the stock market's movements," Liang said after Wednesday's market close.
"It will not issue more and fewer NCDs simply because the stock market rises or falls," Liang said.
Liang said banking system's liquidity remains fairly loose, prompting the central bank to mop up excess funds.
On Thursday, the island's benchmark stock index gained 51.15 points or 0.61 percent to close at 8,492.67.
